title: "Modeling approach"
guide-section: "Reference"

The app fits a single-metric **weighted quadratic aging curve** for
each player.

## The model

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 7
%%| fig-align: 'center'
%%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': { 'fontFamily': 'monospace', "fontSize":"20px", "darkMode":false}}}%%

flowchart TD
    S[/"Seasons<br>Age, metric, PA or IP"/]
    N{"3 or more<br>seasons?"}
    X("No fit")
    W("WLS fit<br>y ~ Age + Age²")
    B{"β₂ < 0?"}
    PK("Peak age<br>-β₁ / (2·β₂)")
    NP("No peak marker")
    CI("95% confidence band")
    S --> N
    N -->|"no"| X
    N -->|"yes"| W
    W --> B
    B -->|"yes"| PK
    B -->|"no"| NP
    W --> CI

style N fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF,rx:5,ry:5
style X fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF,rx:5,ry:5
style W fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF,rx:5,ry:5
style B fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF,rx:5,ry:5
style PK fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF,rx:5,ry:5
style NP fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF,rx:5,ry:5
style CI fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF,rx:5,ry:5
```

For seasons indexed by Age, weighted by playing time:

```
y = β₀ + β₁·Age + β₂·Age² + ε
```

Implementation: `statsmodels.api.WLS(y, X, weights=w).fit()`, with
weights equal to PA (batters) or IP (pitchers). Seasons with more
playing time pull the curve harder than partial seasons.

## Why weighted

A 90-PA September call-up and a 700-PA full season carry the same
arithmetic information to ordinary least squares. However, they're
not equally informative about the player's true ability. Weighting by PA
pushes the fit toward seasons that contain more signal.

## Peak age

When β₂ < 0, the parabola opens downward and there's a real maximum.
Setting the derivative to zero gives the peak age in closed form:

```
Age* = -β₁ / (2·β₂)
```

That's the value the app marks with a dashed vertical line and labels
*Peak: ##.#*.

When β₂ ≥ 0, the curve is flat or concave-up, and the app suppresses
the peak marker. This shape usually signals an unfinished or unusual
career.

## Confidence band

`get_prediction(X).summary_frame(alpha=0.05)` produces a 95% mean
prediction interval at each input age. The shaded ribbon spans
`mean_ci_lower` to `mean_ci_upper`. It widens at the edges of the
career, where fewer seasons constrain the fit.

## Career summary

`summarize_career()` returns:

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 7
%%| fig-align: 'center'
%%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': { 'fontFamily': 'monospace', "fontSize":"20px", "darkMode":false}}}%%

flowchart TD
    D[/"Career seasons"/]
    F[["fit_player_curve()"]]
    S[["summarize_career()"]]
    subgraph G1["<strong>Summary dict</strong>"]
        M("weighted_mean")
        B("best_season")
        P("peak_age")
        W("total_weight")
    end
    T("Career Summary table")
    D --> S
    F -->|"peak_age"| S
    S --> G1
    G1 --> T

style G1 fill:#FFFFFF,color:#000000,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px,rx:10,ry:10
style F fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF,rx:5,ry:5
style S fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF,rx:5,ry:5
style M fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF,rx:5,ry:5
style B fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF,rx:5,ry:5
style P fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF,rx:5,ry:5
style W fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF,rx:5,ry:5
style T fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF,rx:5,ry:5
```

| Field            | What it is                                                  |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `weighted_mean`  | Career rate stat, weighted by the same PA/IP as the fit.    |
| `best_season`    | The season with the highest `y_col` (Season, Age, value).   |
| `peak_age`       | Closed-form peak from the fit (or `None` if non-concave).   |
| `total_weight`   | Career total of PA or IP.                                   |

This dict feeds the one-row summary table in the UI.

## Assumptions and caveats

* **A single quadratic shape** describes the arc. The model fits
  bimodal arcs poorly (injury-recovery careers, mid-career position
  changes, knuckleballers).
* **Weights are exogenous.** A manager who benches a struggling player
  reduces that player's PA. Lower PA biases the fit slightly toward
  years the player was healthy and effective.
* **No era adjustments.** The fit treats a 1908 OPS the same as a 2019
  OPS. See [Limitations](08-limitations.qmd) for more.
